0.0.n: お adds a polite, friendly touch to 話.

0.2.n: This is part of the story’s title, おむすびころりん.

0.3.n: This is only part of ころりん, a playful word suggesting something rolling over.

0.4.n: りん completes ころりん; it has no separate meaning here.

1.0.n: Repeated as 昔々, this is a traditional opening for a folktale.

1.3.n: Before a place or time word, ある introduces something unspecified.

1.4.n: あるところ is a typical folktale expression that leaves the location unnamed.

1.5.n: に marks the place where the old man lived.

1.6.n: This noun describes someone who works diligently.

1.7.n: で links the noun description 働き者 to the next description, 優しい.

1.8.n: This adjective directly describes おじいさん.

1.9.n: Here it refers warmly to an elderly man, not necessarily someone’s grandfather.

1.10.n: が identifies the old man as the person who lived there.

1.11.n: 住む becomes 住んでいました, a polite past form describing an ongoing living situation.

2.0.n: ある introduces an unspecified day in the story.

2.1.n: ある日 is a common expression for introducing when a story event happens.

2.3.n: This refers to the elderly man already introduced.

2.4.n: は makes the old man the topic of this sentence.

2.5.n: This names the destination of his outing.

2.6.n: に marks the mountain as the destination.

2.7.n: Japanese nouns do not need a special plural ending.

2.8.n: を marks the chestnuts as what he will pick up.

2.9.n: 拾い is the form of 拾う used before に to express the purpose of going somewhere.

2.10.n: に after 拾い marks the purpose of going out.

2.11.n: This plain verb form comes before こと in the expression for deciding to do something.

2.12.n: こと turns 出かける into an action that can be discussed as a thing.

2.13.n: に belongs to ことにする, the pattern used to express a decision.

2.14.n: しました is polite past する; together with ことに, it expresses having made a decision.

3.1.n: 今 combines with から to indicate the starting time.

3.2.n: から marks now as the starting point for setting off.

3.3.n: The plain form 行く comes before と to set up a condition.

3.4.n: と links leaving now with its expected result: arriving around noon.

3.5.n: This is what exists on the mountain described next.

3.6.n: の replaces が inside a description before a noun: 栗のある山.

3.7.n: ある expresses existence and helps describe a mountain where chestnuts grow.

3.8.n: 栗のある describes this noun as a place with chestnuts.

3.9.n: に marks the destination reached with 着く.

3.10.n: 着く directly describes 頃, specifying the time of arrival.

3.11.n: After a verb, 頃 indicates approximately when that action happens.

3.12.n: にゃ is a colloquial contraction of には, marking and highlighting the arrival time.

3.13.n: あ lengthens にゃ to にゃあ, giving the speech an old-fashioned, folksy sound.

3.15.n: Here 昼 refers to midday rather than daytime in general.

3.16.n: に marks the resulting state or time with なる.

3.17.n: 昼になる describes the time reaching noon.

4.1.n: The same word can refer to one rice ball or several, depending on context.

4.2.n: を marks the rice balls as what has been prepared.

4.3.n: 作る in て-form plus ある shows that something was deliberately prepared and remains ready.

4.4.n: から gives the reason for the plan that follows.

4.6.n: それ refers back to the prepared rice balls, without marking singular or plural.

4.7.n: を marks the rice balls referred to by それ as what he will eat.

4.8.n: The て-form of 食べる connects eating with the next planned action.

4.10.n: たんと is an old-fashioned, folksy way to express a large amount.

4.11.n: たんと indicates that he intends to gather a large quantity.

4.12.n: を marks the chestnuts as what he intends to gather.

4.13.n: 拾おう is the intention form of 拾う; here the speaker is making a plan for himself.

0.tip: ころりん is one playful rolling expression, even though the subtitle splits it into two tappable pieces.

1.lit: Long, long ago, in a certain place, a hardworking and kind old man was living.
1.tip: で links a noun-based description to another description, letting 働き者 and 優しい describe the same person.

2.lit: One day, the old man decided to go out to the mountain to gather chestnuts.
2.tip: A plain verb followed by ことにしました means someone decided to do that action.

3.lit: If I go from now, around the time I reach the mountain with chestnuts, it will become noon.
3.tip: にゃあ is a folksy contraction of には, not a separate word about cats.

4.lit: Because rice balls have been made ready, I’ll eat those and gather lots of chestnuts.
4.tip: てある emphasizes that something was deliberately done beforehand and its result is still ready or in place.
